root_cause.text: snd_cx88_hw_params() in the cx88 ALSA driver failed to unwind the DMA mapping acquired by cx88_alsa_dma_map() when cx88_risc_databuffer() returned an error, causing a resource leak on the error path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds cx88_alsa_dma_unmap(chip) only in the ret < 0 error branch after cx88_risc_databuffer(), and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state this is needed to release the resource acquired by cx88_alsa_dma_map().

intent_record.intent_summary: Unmap ALSA DMA resources when RISC buffer setup fails in `snd_cx88_hw_params()` to fix error-path resource leakage.
intent_record.what: The change wraps the existing `if (ret < 0)` check in braces and adds a call to `cx88_alsa_dma_unmap(chip);` before jumping to the `error` label when `cx88_risc_databuffer()` returns a negative error code.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if RISC data buffer setup fails, the driver now explicitly unmaps previously mapped ALSA DMA resources before taking the error path, preventing leaked or stale DMA mappings during hardware parameter setup failure.

grouping_result.intent: Unmap ALSA DMA resources when RISC buffer setup fails in `snd_cx88_hw_params()` to fix error-path resource leakage.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the stated root cause by unmapping ALSA DMA resources in snd_cx88_hw_params() when RISC buffer setup fails, addressing the error-path DMA mapping leak.

candidates.rationale: When cx88_risc_databuffer() fails, this jump takes the error path without first unwinding the DMA mapping established earlier by cx88_alsa_dma_map(), directly causing the resource leak.
This condition triggers the faulty error path after cx88_risc_databuffer() failure; combined with the subsequent jump, it exposes the missing DMA unmap cleanup.

This call can fail after DMA resources have already been mapped, and the surrounding pre-fix logic does not unwind those mappings on failure, making this the operation that enters the leaking error path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This jump sends execution to the generic error path after cx88_risc_databuffer() fails, but in the pre-fix code it does so without first unwinding the DMA mapping previously acquired by cx88_alsa_dma_map(), directly causing the resource leak.

V4L/DVB (6083): cx88-alsa: Rework buffer handling

Rework the way the DMA buffer is handled and IRQs are generated.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full allocation/mapping/error flow. The vulnerable construct is present: after successful DMA setup with `videobuf_dma_init_kernel(...)` at lines 403-406 and successful PCI DMA mapping with `videobuf_pci_dma_map(chip->pci,&buf->vb.dma)` at lines 408-410, the code calls `cx88_risc_databuffer(...)` at lines 412-413. If that call fails, line 415 does `goto error;`, and the `error:` block at lines 429-431 only does `kfree(buf); return ret;`. There is no unwind of the DMA mapping or DMA buffer resources before freeing `buf`. Thus, when `cx88_risc_databuffer()` returns an error after the mapping was acquired, the mapping is leaked. The fix is not present because the error path lacks any call to unmap/free the DMA resources associated with `buf->vb.dma` before `kfree(buf)`.
